title: Vendor Onsite Audit & Assessment Addendum (Template, v0.3)
content:
Purpose:
This Addendum ("Addendum") supplements the underlying agreement between Redwood Inference ("Customer") and [Vendor] ("Vendor") and documents the parties' agreement regarding Vendor onsite audits and compliance assessments of services used to process or store Customer data. This template is intended for negotiation as an annex to the Master Services Agreement, Statement of Work, or Data Processing Agreement where Vendor hosts or processes regulated or sensitive data for Redwood Inference.

Scope:
1. Applicability: This Addendum applies to all systems, locations and third-party subprocessor facilities used by Vendor to provide services under the Parties' agreement where those systems store, process or transmit Customer Data.
2. Audit Types: Audits covered include: (a) remote documentation review; (b) technical evidence collection (logs, configurations); and (c) onsite assessments (facility walkthroughs, interviews, sample testing).

Definitions:
- "Customer Data": as defined in the underlying agreement.
- "Confidential Information": as defined in the underlying agreement.
- "Audit Window": the period during which the audit will be conducted, as agreed per Section 4.

Audit Rights and Frequency:
1. Customer Rights: Upon reasonable written notice (not less than 30 days), Customer (or a mutually agreed independent auditor) may:
   a. Perform a remote or onsite assessment no more than once per 12-month period, unless a material security incident, regulatory inquiry, or repeated non-compliance is discovered.
   b. Review policies, procedures, technical controls, and evidence reasonably necessary to verify Vendor's compliance with the Agreement.
2. Exceptions: Customer may request an additional audit sooner than the 12-month interval if there is: (i) a material security incident; (ii) evidence of a breach of this Agreement; or (iii) a regulatory request reasonably requiring verification.

Scheduling and Logistics:
1. Notice and Coordination: Customer will provide proposed dates and a preliminary scope no less than 30 days prior to the requested onsite assessment date. Parties will coordinate to minimize operational disruption; Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate.
2. Duration: Typical onsite assessments shall not exceed two consecutive business days unless otherwise agreed in writing.
3. Attendees: Onsite audit attendees must be identified in advance and may include Customer's security/compliance personnel or a third-party auditor provided they execute Vendor's reasonable confidentiality and access agreements.

Audit Scope and Activities:
1. Areas of Review: Physical security, logical/technical controls, access management, encryption and key management practices, secure development and change management evidence, incident response readiness, backup and restore procedures, and applicable compliance artifacts (e.g., SOC2, ISO certificates).
2. Sampling: Audit activities will use sampling techniques; specific data subject records will not be accessed unless necessary and only with express prior consent and specific scope limits.
3. Tooling and Access: If specialized tooling (e.g., vulnerability scanners) is required, Customer will provide details in advance and obtain Vendor approval. Any active scanning will be scheduled and limited to agreed targets and windows.

Data Handling, Confidentiality, and Minimization:
1. Confidentiality: All information accessed during the audit shall be treated as Confidential Information per the underlying agreement. The auditor shall not retain copies of Customer Data beyond what is strictly necessary for the audit report.
2. Data Minimization: Customer shall limit requests for production data and will first seek non-production artifacts (configuration, logs with redaction, system diagrams). When production data is required, both parties must agree on redaction and least-privilege access.
3. Findings Distribution: Audit findings will be shared only with Vendor personnel with a need-to-know and Customer stakeholders, and any third-party auditor bound by confidentiality obligations.

Remediation and Follow-up:
1. Findings Classification: Findings will be classified as Critical, High, Medium, or Low, with descriptions and evidence.
2. Remediation Plan: Vendor shall propose a remediation plan for Critical/High findings within 10 business days that includes root cause analysis, remediation steps, timeline, and verification approach.
3. Verification: Customer may require a targeted follow-up review to validate remediation. Subsequent follow-ups shall be coordinated and, absent material issues, limited in number.

Costs and Reasonable Allocation:
1. Routine Audits: Costs for routine annual audits are borne by Customer, except where the audit is triggered by a material incident or repeated non-compliance, in which case Vendor shall bear reasonable costs for Customer's incremental auditor expenses.
2. Travel and Onsite Expenses: Customer or its auditor's travel expenses for onsite assessments shall be borne by Customer unless negotiated otherwise.

Limitations and Protections for Vendor:
1. Operational Impact: Audit activities will be conducted to avoid undue operational impact. Vendor may suspend access that materially threatens service integrity, subject to reasonable notice.
2. Proprietary Information: Auditors will not be permitted to access Vendor proprietary tooling source code or internal pricing models unless mutually agreed and under strict protective measures.

Integration with Compliance Programs and Evidence:
1. Existing Reports: Where Vendor maintains recent independent third-party reports (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001) or other certifications, these shall be accepted in lieu of portions of the audit scope where they are relevant and current.
2. Evidence Retention: Audit reports and evidence shall be retained consistent with the Confidentiality and Data Retention provisions of the underlying agreement.

Incident-Triggered Acceleration:
If an incident materially affecting Customer Data occurs, Customer may request an expedited audit with no less than 5 business days' notice. Vendor shall cooperate and provide prioritized access to relevant evidence. Cost allocation for incident-triggered audits follows Section 6.1.

Termination Right for Material Non-Compliance:
If an audit identifies material, unremediated non-compliance with obligations related to Customer Data, Customer may exercise rights under the underlying agreement, including suspension, termination for cause, or other remedies, subject to any cure periods required by that agreement.

Governing Law and Dispute Resolution:
This Addendum shall be governed by the governing law of the underlying agreement. Disputes arising from this Addendum will follow the dispute resolution process set forth in the underlying agreement, with escalation to designated security and legal leads before formal dispute processes are invoked.

Signatures:
The parties agree to the terms of this Addendum as of the Effective Date below.

Customer: Redwood Inference
Name: _______________________

Appendix A — Example Evidence Checklist (non-exhaustive):
- Physical access logs and access control policies
- Network segmentation diagrams and firewall rules
- Privileged access review and least-privilege evidence
- Patch management records for in-scope systems
- Backup schedules and restore test reports
- Incident response runbooks and recent incident summaries
- Third-party assessment reports (SOC 2, ISO, penetration tests)
- Change management tickets and deployment approvals

Notes and Negotiation Considerations: This template is intended to balance Customer verification needs with Vendor operational realities. Suggested negotiation points: frequency cap (annual vs. bi-annual), limitation on days for onsite presence, redaction and data minimization procedures, cost-sharing on incident-triggered audits, and acceptance of current third-party assurances to reduce duplication.

Document history: v0.1 initial draft (legal intake) 2024-06-18; v0.2 incorporated SRE feedback 2024-07-02; v0.3 updated cost allocation and scheduling windows 2024-07-12.
